newsitem.title: JAPAN: Grim, unsolved murder shakes parents in Japan city.
newsitem.headline: Grim, unsolved murder shakes parents in Japan city.

text.p: One month after a schoolboy was beheaded by a killer who has threatened to strike again, nerves are fraying among parents in the western Japan city of Kobe.

As police continue their hunt for the killer, parents are suffering from nervous tension worrying about their children's safety, Kyodo news agency quoted an official at a neighbourhood association as saying.
"The tension continues on and, even more than the children, the parents' nerves are fraying. I don't know if they'll still be OK if the summer carries on this way," the official said.
The macabre killing and beheading of 11-year-old Jun Hase has almost paralysed the local community, which is still not fully recovered from the 1995 earthquake in which 6,000 people died.

Few children or mothers can be seen on the streets of Jun's neighbourhood and some parents have even allowed terrorised children to quit evening cram school classes that many usually attend, according to the schools.
Local supermarkets report that sales of children's clothes, toys and stationery items targeted at children have plunged as children stay at home.

The murder, which shocked a nation that prides itself on public safety, occurred just before the National Police Agency said that crimes against younger children were on the rise for a second consecutive year. Jun left his home in Kobe on May 24 to visit his grandfather. Three days later the sixth-grader's severed head was found at the foot of the iron gate of a nearby junior high school. Inside his mouth was a note saying the murderer enjoyed killing and planned to strike again.
Jun's body was discovered in a forest near Tainohata Elementary School, where he was a pupil.
A school spokeswoman said in telephone interview that the number of guards at the school had been doubled and staff were trying to continue activities as before.
"The children don't seem to be scared any more but if you ask them they'll tell you they are... We're trying to carry on as normal," she said.

Teachers and parents alike are counting the days until school summer holidays begin on July 19 while police puzzle over leads linking the killing to horror movies, which authorities have refused to identify.

In another lead, police said two weeks ago an open-access Internet page had appeared in Kobe last February displaying a message similar to the note found in Jun's mouth, including the words "wine", "devil" and "rose" in red.

The cryptic note found with the body spoke of killing "dirty vegetables" in what police said was a reference to people or children, and resembled messages written by the "Zodiac" killer who went on a killing spree in California beginning in 1966.

The Zodiac killer, who was never caught, sent taunting notes to the police and media every time he struck with a cross drawn inside a circle similar to a mark found on a cryptic message attached to Jun's head.

In March, two young schoolgirls were attacked by a knife-wielding man near the school where the head was found, and one 10-year-old died. Police said there was no evidence so far that the cases were linked.
